about: The Cosmic Atlas: one record per stage of the journey. The page reads its text, labels, sources and camera framing from here. Ages are years after the Big Bang as [earliest, latest]; null means the stage is not tied to one epoch. 'transition' says how the journey leaves a stage: a morph, or a zoom in or out by 'depth' e-folds of scale.

events.title: Primordial energy
events.label: model
events.note: Hot, dense and almost uniform. Space itself is expanding, and tiny fluctuations will seed everything that follows. At 380,000 years the universe turns transparent.
events.sound: sub-bass drone, a growling filtered saw, grainy noise and a rising wall of harmonics

events.title: Structure emerges
events.label: observed
events.era: hundreds of millions of years on
events.note: Gravity pulls dark matter and gas into filaments and nodes. Galaxy surveys map this web; the shape drawn here is procedural, not survey data.
events.sound: glassy open fifths that shimmer, with a breath of high air

events.title: A city of galaxies
events.label: observed
events.note: The bright knot resolves into dozens of young galaxies with empty space between them, pulled together by gravity. Webb sees clusters like this forming, such as the Spiderweb.
events.sound: a quiet open pad with scattered bell notes, one per galaxy

events.title: A young galaxy blazes
events.label: observed
events.era: about 10 billion years ago, when quasars peaked
events.scale: tens of thousands of light-years, jets far beyond
events.note: Inside the cluster, one smudge up close: a young galaxy with giant clumps of new stars, tidal tails, and a core outshining everything, firing twin jets.
events.sound: a bright chord pulsing hard, a deep throb and a jet-like hiss

events.title: A galaxy like ours
events.label: observed
events.era: over the next several billion years
events.note: Mergers calm and the gas settles into a barred spiral like the Milky Way: a dense bulge, arms that thin towards the edge, dust lanes and pink star-forming regions.
events.sound: a warm, slowly breathing D minor 9 pad

events.title: The dark heart
events.label: observed
events.era: at the centre of nearly every large galaxy
events.scale: ours fits inside Mercury's orbit; the largest outsize the solar system
events.note: A supermassive black hole. Telescopes have imaged the ring of light around two of them and tracked stars orbiting ours. This view is procedural.
events.sound: a slow heartbeat at the edge of hearing, deep rumble, one eerie high tone

events.title: Pillars of creation
events.label: observed
events.note: Back in a spiral arm: pillars of cold gas and dust, eroded by hot young stars above. Hydrogen glows red, oxygen green-teal. New stars form in the dense tips.
events.sound: breathy, vowel-like noise, as if the pillars were singing, over a soft pad

events.title: A cloud collapses
events.label: observed
events.era: 4.6 billion years ago, for our Sun
events.note: One knot falls in on itself. Spin flattens the infalling gas into a disc, and the newborn star fires narrow jets from its poles.
events.sound: a low saw straining against a closing filter, the hiss of infall

events.title: A star ignites
events.label: observed
events.note: Fusion begins. Around the star, dust settles into a disc with rings and gaps, like those ALMA imaged around the young star HL Tauri.
events.sound: the first major chord, bright and warm

events.title: Worlds form
events.label: model
events.era: the next 100 million years or so
events.note: Dust drifts along each ring and gathers into clumps that grow into planets: small rocky ones close in, giants beyond the frost line. Sizes are exaggerated.
events.sound: a slow music-box arpeggio over a soft pad, like orbits ticking round

events.title: The star sheds its shell
events.label: model
events.era: about 5 billion years from now, for our Sun
events.note: Our Sun will swell into a red giant, swallow its innermost planets and push its outer layers into space. Older Sun-like stars are doing this now.
events.sound: low, slow and swelling: a minor third that sighs

events.title: The universe looks back
events.label: observed
events.era: about 5 billion years from now; the Helix shows it today
events.note: What our Sun will leave behind. The Helix Nebula, about 650 light-years away, is a real shell like this. The shape is procedural; the eye is our reading.
events.sound: resolution: a still D major 9 with high shimmer
